newsitem.title: USA: Macrochem says gel test results positive.
newsitem.headline: Macrochem says gel test results positive.

text.p: MacroChem Corp said on Tuesday preliminary results from an ongoing Phase I/II clinical trial of its topical gel treatment for erectile dysfunction or impotence were positive.

"We are highly encouraged by the preliminary results suggesting significant erectile responses at the lower doses," Carlos Samour, MacroChem's chairman and scientific director, said. "With the results of this interim analysis, MacroChem is continuing its Phase I/II clinical trials with plans to expand clinical development of this potential product."

MacroChem's treatment is a gel combining alprostadil, the only U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved drug for erectile dysfunction, and SEPA, the company's proprietary absorption enchancer for transdermal drug delivery.
The company said the objective of this clinical trial was to determine the effective and safe dosage range of the topically-applied formulation.
It has been estimated that 10 to 20 million men in the United States suffer from erectile dysfunction, MacroChem said.
